idea: Property technology landscape research for VCs and corporates
buyer: VCs and corporate strategy teams in real estate
pain: Nobody assessing proptech understands both construction reality and investment logic
v1: One landscape report on a proptech segment
verdict: Good fit and fees, but proptech VC activity has contracted sharply and buyers are few.

why.distribution: VCs are adjacent to her network rather than in it.
why.demand: Inferred; VC research budgets have contracted with the funding environment.
why.fmf: Assessing whether a construction technology actually works needs her exact combination.
why.defensibility: Accumulated landscape knowledge helps but is easily matched.
why.leverage: Reports can be resold to multiple buyers in the same segment.
why.tailwind: Proptech funding is well off its peak.
why.ceiling: £15k x 13 reports = £195k, in a segment where the buyer count is small and shrinking.

ceiling_arithmetic: £15k x 13 reports = £195k. The buyer universe for proptech landscape research in the UK is perhaps 20-30 firms and their budgets have shrunk. Realistic: 3-4 = £45-60k.
carries: A genuine analytical edge on whether construction technologies actually work.
kills: A small and contracting buyer universe with reduced research budgets.
test: Ask three proptech VCs what research they bought last year.
test_pass: They name recent purchases and a gap.
test_fail: They say they do it in-house or stopped buying.
